— uses the OS adaptive brightness service (ADAPTBRIGHT). Slow, opaque, single hard-coded curve, no learning.

— reads the ALS directly. One-Euro-filtered lux signal, log lux → brightness curve, sustained-change requirement before reacting (won't twitch on transient flashes), direction-aware response (brightens quickly when entering a darker space, dims slowly to avoid flicker), smooth eased transitions instead of stepped jumps, lux-ratio override hold (your manual adjustment sticks until ambient changes by 2×). Each time you nudge the slider, the helper learns your preferred offset for that ambient range (six log-spaced lux buckets) and biases future predictions toward what you picked. Switching to Helper turns Windows ADAPTBRIGHT off so the two don't fight.

attrs.Text: Power button behavior and idle timers
GoTweaks feature - not a Windows setting, since Windows has no built-in idle-to-hibernate timer
Windows' own Sleep timer can still fire first

Windows' default Sleep (Modern Standby) sometimes drains the battery from background wake-ups or fails to resume cleanly. Hibernate saves the session to disk and fully powers off, which is closer to how SteamOS suspends and tends to be more reliable - at the cost of a slightly slower resume. Setting the Power Button and Hibernate Timeout options above to Hibernate (and disabling Windows' Sleep timer) is the recommended change.
